# Published engine interoperability vectors

These expected values were generated by `@railgun-community/engine` **9.6.0**,
source commit `6e2614d53a106dd62abad91e7ce03ee4a3956138`. They are not generated by
the Rust implementation under test. The fixture records hashes of the engine's
four directly imported modules; the generator uses its actual derivation,
key/signature, address and TXID functions.

**All credentials are from the well-known public mnemonic
`test test test test test test test test test test test junk`. Never fund these
accounts.** Fixture generation opens no wallet, database, RPC, indexer or POI
service, and refuses accidental HTTP/socket requests.

The three account indices (0, 1, 65535) cover spending/viewing derivation inputs,
spending/viewing public keys, master keys, chain-agnostic/mainnet/Sepolia address
encodings and deterministic EdDSA-Poseidon signatures. Messages include zero,
one, 42, a value above `u64::MAX`, and the last BN254 scalar-field element.
TXIDs cover 1x1, 1x2, 2x3 and 13x13 input/output lists, including protocol zero
padding, order and bound-parameter binding. These are offline protocol facts,
not deployment, account-custody, hardware or complete transaction qualification.

The external-signer test stores no spending key in its signer implementation.
It returns independently generated reference signatures, verifies them with the
public key and propagates a declined request. It does not claim a hardware test.

## Run

```sh
cd crates
cargo test --locked -p kohaku-railgun --lib interop_tests
```

Rust CI reads the committed JSON and needs no Node installation or network.

## Regenerate

Install the exact published engine 9.6.0 in a separate development directory with
lifecycle scripts disabled and retain its lockfile. The original generation
used the [pinned engine fixture lock](https://github.com/solardev-xyz/railgun-kohaku-adapter/blob/1e555a27df75d662d713b213e8ec71749209cb3e/tools/railgun-runtime-build/scripts/fixtures/railgun-engine/package-lock.json).
That installation is development tooling only, not a Rust runtime dependency.

```sh
node crates/railgun/tests/fixtures/engine-interoperability/generate.cjs \
  /absolute/engine-fixture/node_modules/@railgun-community/engine > /absolute/new-vectors.json
```

Compare the new JSON to `vectors.json`; do not overwrite reference expectations
with values computed by the Rust implementation just to make a test pass.
